title.fa: پولیس و خانه: حیطهٔ عمومی و خصوصی نزد آرنت
title.en: Polis and household: the public and private realms in Arendt
title.nl: Polis en huishouden: het publieke en private domein bij Arendt

summary.fa: آرنت می‌گوید در فهم یونانی زندگی خانه قلمرو ضرورت بود و پولیس قلمرو آزادی، گفتار و عمل. به نظر او ترجمهٔ لاتینی و مدرن «سیاسی» به «اجتماعی» این تمایز را محو کرد.
summary.en: Arendt says that in Greek understanding the household was the realm of necessity and the polis the realm of freedom, speech and action. She argues that the Latin and modern rendering of 'political' as 'social' erased this distinction.
summary.nl: Volgens Arendt was het huishouden het rijk van de noodzaak en de polis dat van vrijheid, spraak en handelen; het moderne 'sociale' heeft dit onderscheid uitgewist.

text.fa: به روایت آرنت، تأسیس پولیس برای هر شهروند «زندگی دوم» آورد: او به دو مرتبه تعلق دارد، آنچه از آنِ خود اوست (idion) و آنچه مشترک است (koinon).
text.en: On Arendt's account the founding of the polis gave each citizen a 'second life': he belongs to two orders, what is his own (idion) and what is common (koinon).
text.nl: On Arendt's account the founding of the polis gave each citizen a 'second life': he belongs to two orders, what is his own (idion) and what is common (koinon).

text.fa: در خانه، نیازهای حیات (خوراک، زادوولد) فرمان می‌راندند و خشونت و فرمانروایی بر بردگان برای چیرگی بر ضرورت موجه بود؛ آزادی تنها در حیطهٔ سیاسی بود و چیرگی بر ضرورت در خانه شرط آن به‌شمار می‌رفت.
text.en: In the household necessity ruled, and force and command over slaves were seen as justified ways to master necessity; freedom lived only in the political realm, for which mastery of necessity at home was the precondition.
text.nl: In the household necessity ruled, and force and command over slaves were seen as justified ways to master necessity; freedom lived only in the political realm, for which mastery of necessity at home was the precondition.

text.fa: عمل (praxis) و سخن (lexis) دو فعالیتی‌اند که به نظر آرنت زندگی سیاسی را می‌سازند. یافتن واژهٔ درست در زمان درست خود عمل است، و تنها خشونت محض خاموش است.
text.en: Action (praxis) and speech (lexis) are the two activities that, for Arendt, constitute political life. Finding the right words at the right time is itself action, and only sheer violence is mute.
text.nl: Action (praxis) and speech (lexis) are the two activities that, for Arendt, constitute political life. Finding the right words at the right time is itself action, and only sheer violence is mute.

text.fa: او می‌گوید تعریف ارسطو از انسان به‌عنوان حیوان سیاسی و حیوان دارای سخن، نظر رایج پولیس را بیان می‌کرد و ترجمهٔ لاتین آن به «حیوان اجتماعی» (و «حیوان عقلانی») بدفهمی بزرگی است.
text.en: She argues that Aristotle's formulas—political animal and speaking animal—voiced the polis's common view, and that the Latin 'social animal' (and 'rational animal') is a serious misunderstanding.
text.nl: She argues that Aristotle's formulas—political animal and speaking animal—voiced the polis's common view, and that the Latin 'social animal' (and 'rational animal') is a serious misunderstanding.

text.fa: از نظر آرنت، فرمانروایی مطلق و حیطهٔ سیاسی با هم جمع نمی‌شوند؛ قدرت رئیس خانه از قدرت پادشاه «کامل‌تر» نبود بلکه از نوعی دیگر بود (او با استدلال آکویناس مخالف است).
text.en: For Arendt, absolute rule and the political realm are mutually exclusive; the household head's power was not a fuller version of kingly power but a different kind of thing, against Aquinas's comparison.
text.nl: For Arendt, absolute rule and the political realm are mutually exclusive; the household head's power was not a fuller version of kingly power but a different kind of thing, against Aquinas's comparison.

text.fa: او همچنین می‌گوید پولیس حریم خانه را نگه می‌داشت نه از سر احترام به مالکیت خصوصی به معنای مدرن، بلکه چون بی‌داشتن جایی از آنِ خود نمی‌شد در امور جهان شرکت کرد.
text.en: She adds that the polis respected the household not out of respect for private property in the modern sense but because one without a place of one's own could not take part in worldly affairs.
text.nl: She adds that the polis respected the household not out of respect for private property in the modern sense but because one without a place of one's own could not take part in worldly affairs.

text.fa: تصویر آرنت از پولیس آرمانی و گزینشی است: آزادی شهروندان بر کار بردگان و زنان بنا بود، و منتقدان (از جمله فمینیست‌ها) می‌گویند جداکردن تیز «ضرورت» از «آزادی» حیطهٔ خصوصی را از سیاست بیرون می‌گذارد. مورخان نیز با ادعای او دربارهٔ جدایی کامل اقتصاد و سیاست در آتن موافق نیستند.
text.en: Arendt's picture of the polis is idealised and selective: citizens' freedom rested on the labour of slaves and women, and critics (including feminist scholars) argue that a sharp necessity/freedom divide excludes the private sphere from politics. Historians also dispute that economy and politics were wholly separate in Athens.
text.nl: Arendt's picture of the polis is idealised and selective: citizens' freedom rested on the labour of slaves and women, and critics (including feminist scholars) argue that a sharp necessity/freedom divide excludes the private sphere from politics. Historians also dispute that economy and politics were wholly separate in Athens.
